quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, what should you do?

options.text: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks is dangerous.
Do not cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Cross the tracks by riding on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, ride straight within your lane. Do not turn to cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle because you could end up in another lane of traffic.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Only at night.
Only during the day.
You should not wear it.
Both day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both day and night.
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps others see you in any lighting condition. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing during daytime too.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the center portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
Weave among all three portions of the lane as they pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle raises your crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to merge back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Give you a poor view of road hazards.
Invite other vehicles to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. Do not ride in another driver's blind spot.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you stay in your lane?

options.text: Toward the right side of your lane.
Toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left more often.
Use your rearview mirrors more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane away from the parked cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. If oncoming traffic is present, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, what should you do?

options.text: Let the load move freely.
Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not shift and affect the motorcycle's handling. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to reduce tipping of the sidecar nose during sharp left turns.

questions.question: When making a turn, what happens to your ability to stop?

options.text: There is less traction available for stopping.
There is more traction available for stopping.
Stopping is the same as on a straightaway.
You should never attempt to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less traction available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but do it carefully. When a motorcycle is leaning, less traction is available for stopping because some traction is being used for turning.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT needed for an effective eye or face shield?

options.text: It should be free of scratches.
It should resist penetration.
It should fasten securely.
It should be airtight.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be airtight.
questions.explanation: Good eye protection and face shields must be free of scratches, resist penetration, give a clear side view, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. They should also fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.question: Why is riding alongside another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The driver may change lanes without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Stay where you are so you don't surprise the driver.
Wave at the other driver to get their attention.
Slow down to get out of the blind spot.
Pull over to the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to get out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, speed up quickly or slow down to leave the spot.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?

options.text: Stopping will be easier.
Stopping will take longer.
You cannot stop.
Stopping is about the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to the motorcycle. More braking force is needed to stop. Downhill riding also makes stopping harder. Both factors together mean longer stopping distances.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your normal space cushion.
Brake later than usual.
Ride a little slower than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little slower than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and makes your motorcycle sit lower. Ride slower, especially through curves and bumps. The extra weight also means longer acceleration, braking, and stopping times. Keep more space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, what should you do?

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.
Always ride in the right part of the lane.
Be flexible and consider many factors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible and consider many factors.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose the position where other drivers can see you best and where you have space around you to stay safe.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to driving a car. However, what is different?

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: Being seen is more important on a motorcycle than in a car. Motorcycles are smaller and can easily hide in another vehicle's blind spot. Drivers may not notice you even if they look.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle into the slippery section to stay balanced.
Keep your speed to improve grip.
Don't worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid slippery roads. If you cannot avoid one, keep your motorcycle upright and ride as slowly as possible.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Always use both brakes.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake on wet roads.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what road conditions are like.

questions.question: To carry a passenger safely, what may you need to adjust on your motorcycle?

options.text: The shocks.
The handlebars.
The brakes.
The throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shocks.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so you may need to adjust the shocks. The motorcycle will sit at a different angle, so also adjust the headlight and mirrors.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what is the best thing to do?

options.text: Don't worry about it.
Change lanes safely and let them pass.
Speed up.
Get off the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes safely and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only encourage them to tailgate at higher speeds.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is less effective than the rear brake.
It is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe when used correctly.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Both your eyes and your face.
Your face, but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your face.
Neither your face nor your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield is needed to protect your entire face in a crash.

questions.question: How should a group ride when entering a curve?

options.text: In a single-file line.
In a staggered formation.
In pairs.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Groups should ride in a staggered formation normally, but must switch to single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Use the brake on the flat tire.
Use both brakes.
Do not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat, if you are sure which one that is.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white background and black text or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When you stop, how should you use the brakes?

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front or rear brake, not both.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together every time you slow down or stop.
